title: optimize cpu request path: reduce serialization + thread-pinning + per-shard pools
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: High-concurrency production traces and perf-canary runs showed CPU-side bottlenecks in the request path: a hot global serialization lock, excessive cross-socket thread migration, and thread-pool contention during KV cache-heavy workloads. These manifested as elevated p95/p99 latency under 2k-10k concurrent QPS, and increased system CPU utilization. This PR targets the CPU request path (serialization, scheduling, and thread pools) with minimal semantic changes to user-facing APIs.
changes_summary:
- Remove single global request serialization lock: introduce per-shard locks and a fast-path lock-free queue for common KV-cache-hit responses.
- Rework request worker pool: per-core worker pools with optional work-stealing to reduce contention and improve locality.
- Add explicit thread pinning policy and runtime-configurable affinity sets to keep request workers pinned to sockets/cores; provide safe fallback to OS scheduling.
- Move expensive proto/json serialization of large responses into a dedicated serialization worker stage that runs downstream of CPU-critical scheduling; small responses still use inline fast-path serialization.
- Add microbenchmarks, end-to-end canary tests, and NUMA-aware perf harnesses.
- Add feature flag (perf.cpu_request_path_v2) and runtime knobs for affinity and pool sizes.
commits: Initial refactor: per-shard request queues and lock-free fast-path (mch-1)
Add thread affinity/ pinning as configurable policy (mch-3)
Move serialization to dedicated stage + tests (mch-4)
Fix: conservative fallback when affinity unavailable (mch-6)
review_comments: Diego Alvarez: flagged a potential NUMA imbalance when pinning all request workers to the same socket — requested a runtime knob and test showing cross-socket fallback.
Maya Chen: added runtime config (affinity.fallback_policy) and NUMA-aware placement logic; added test that simulates asymmetric socket load and verifies fallback.
Priya Natarajan: requested microbenchmark numbers and CI perf harness results before approving; noted a possible impact to pre-existing autoscaling heuristics.
Maya Chen: included 10-run median/p95 numbers from perf-canary; documented autoscaler implications and default conservative pool sizes.
Liam O'Connor: approved after CI pass and perf numbers validated on dedicated canary cluster.
ci_summary: CI passed after a single rerun. One flaky unit test (tests/async_io_test) failed on first run; rerun green. Perf-canary runs executed against a dedicated canary cluster: medians p95 improvement 20-35% across target workloads; CPU utilization reduced ~15% for KV-cache heavy traces.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: thread pinning may worsen some multi-tenant setups or interfere with host-level CPU reclaimers. Mitigations: feature off by default, runtime knobs for affinity and per-tenant override, and conservative default pool sizes. Added docs and fallback policy to revert to OS scheduling if measurement indicates imbalance.
release_notes: CPU request path optimizations: reduced p95/p99 latency for high-concurrency workloads by addressing serialization and thread-pool contention. Feature gated under perf.cpu_request_path_v2. See docs/perf/README-cpu-request-path.md for rollout guidance and knobs.
notes_for_operators:
- Toggle via runtime flag: perf.cpu_request_path_v2=false to disable.
- Affinity controls: affinity.policy=auto|socket|none; affinity.fallback_policy=allow_migration|force_fallback.
- Recommended runbook: enable on canary for 24h, monitor p95 latency, CPU steal and load imbalance metrics.
tests_added: integration: tests/request_path_perf_test.cc, unit: runtime/thread_pool_test.cc, e2e: perf/canary/cpu_request_path_bench.py
notes: Small API surface changes restricted to internal runtime config. No user-visible API changes. This PR was coordinated with autoscaler team to ensure no regressions in Dedicated flow.
